plain_title: Container Base Image Backdooring risk at Chat Frontend
mitigation: Apply hardening of all container infrastructures (see for example the CIS-Benchmarks for Docker and Kubernetes and the Docker Bench for Security). Also consider using Google's Distroless base images or otherwise very small base images. Regularly execute container image scans with tools checking the layers for vulnerable components.

title: Missing Cloud Hardening risk at Agent Subnet
plain_title: Missing Cloud Hardening risk at Agent Subnet
mitigation:
Apply hardening of all cloud components and services, taking special care to follow the individual risk descriptions (which depend on the cloud provider tags in the model).

For Amazon Web Services (AWS): Follow the CIS Benchmark for Amazon Web Services (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "PacBot", "CloudSploit", "CloudMapper", "ScoutSuite", or "Prowler AWS CIS Benchmark Tool").
For EC2 and other servers running Amazon Linux, follow the CIS Benchmark for Amazon Linux and switch to IMDSv2.
For S3 buckets follow the Security Best Practices for Amazon S3 at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/dev/security-best-practices.html to avoid accidental leakage.
Also take a look at some of these tools: https://github.com/toniblyx/my-arsenal-of-aws-security-tools

For Microsoft Azure: Follow the CIS Benchmark for Microsoft Azure (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit" or "ScoutSuite").

For Google Cloud Platform: Follow the CIS Benchmark for Google Cloud Computing Platform (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit" or "ScoutSuite").

For Oracle Cloud Platform: Follow the hardening best practices (see also the automated checks of cloud audit tools like "CloudSploit").
check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

title: Unverified Model Supply Chain risk at Model Registry
plain_title: Unverified Model Supply Chain risk at Model Registry
references: OWASP LLM04:2025 Data and Model Poisoning
OWASP ASI04:2026 Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
mitigation: Take models only from trusted sources, pin them by digest and verify their signatures or hashes before they are loaded. Keep a bill of materials of the models and their training data (an ML BOM), prefer formats that cannot run code when loaded (like safetensors), restrict who can write to the model registry, and evaluate a model before it reaches production.

title: Prompt Injection risk at Support Agent
plain_title: Prompt Injection risk at Support Agent
mitigation: Treat everything a model reads as untrusted, including retrieved documents and tool responses: keep instructions apart from data (for example with clearly delimited and labelled content), filter input and output, and give the model and its tools only the permissions the task needs. Require a human approval for actions with side effects, and monitor for injection attempts. See the OWASP GenAI Security Project at https://genai.owasp.org/.

title: Publicly Shared Cloud Snapshot risk at Orders Database
plain_title: Publicly Shared Cloud Snapshot risk at Orders Database
mitigation:
Prevent the public sharing of snapshots and images with a cloud configuration rule that revokes it, and audit the sharing settings regularly. Do not bake credentials into images; see the secrets management cheat sheet at https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Secrets_Management_Cheat_Sheet.html.

For Amazon Web Services (AWS): Turn on block public access for EBS snapshots (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/block-public-access-snapshots.html) and for AMIs (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/block-public-access-to-amis.html) in every region, use the AWS Config managed rules ebs-snapshot-public-restorable-check (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/ebs-snapshot-public-restorable-check.html) and rds-snapshots-public-prohibited (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/config/latest/developerguide/rds-snapshots-public-prohibited.html) with an automatic remediation, and review the snapshot findings of IAM Access Analyzer (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/what-is-access-analyzer.html).
check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

mitigation: Try to use parameter binding to be safe from injection vulnerabilities. When a third-party product is used instead of custom developed software, check if the product applies the proper mitigation and ensure a reasonable patch-level.

title: Unauthenticated MCP Server risk at Support Tools called by Support Agent
plain_title: Unauthenticated MCP Server risk at Support Tools called by Support Agent
references: OWASP ASI02:2026 Tool Misuse and Exploitation
OWASP ASI03:2026 Identity and Privilege Abuse
mitigation: Authenticate every caller of the server, for example with OAuth 2.1 as the MCP specification describes for HTTP transports, and pass on the identity of the user an agent acts for, so that each tool call is authorized for that user. Expose the server only to the agents that need it.
check: Are recommendations from the linked cheat sheet and referenced ASVS chapter applied?

title: Unchecked Deployment risk at Model Registry
plain_title: Unchecked Deployment risk at Model Registry
mitigation: Apply DevSecOps best-practices and use scanning tools to identify vulnerabilities in source- or byte-code,dependencies, container layers, and optionally also via dynamic scans against running test systems.

title: Unguarded Access from Internet of Chat Frontend by Customer Browser via Support Chat
plain_title: Unguarded Access from Internet of Chat Frontend by Customer Browser via Support Chat
mitigation: Encapsulate the asset behind a guarding service, application, or reverse-proxy. For admin maintenance a bastion-host should be used as a jump-server. For file transfer a store-and-forward-host should be used as an indirect file exchange platform.

title: Vector Store Poisoning risk at Knowledge Index used by Support Agent
plain_title: Vector Store Poisoning risk at Knowledge Index used by Support Agent
references: OWASP LLM04:2025 Data and Model Poisoning
OWASP LLM08:2025 Vector and Embedding Weaknesses
OWASP ASI06:2026 Memory and Context Poisoning
mitigation: Ingest only content from vetted sources, record where each entry came from and validate it before it is embedded. Keep the entries of different users and tenants apart with access controls at retrieval time, limit what agents may write into their memory, and review and expire stored entries regularly.
